title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: notes for the 1976 IHÉS talk on the divided-power de Rham complex. Grothendieck is setting up linear algebra of a k-module M through the functor V(M): A ↦ Hom_k(M, A), which is contravariant in M. On the previous page, coalgebra structures on M correspond to bilinear composition laws on V(M), and projective limits of coalgebras are discussed. The top line of this page completes that sentence: the axioms of associativity, unit and commutativity 'passent à la limite'.

(1) Gradings. Let 𝕀 be a set (a script/barred I, not ℤ). A grading of type 𝕀 on M is a direct-sum decomposition M ≅ ⊕_{α∈𝕀} M_α into submodules. Since V turns direct sums into products, this is the same as a product decomposition V(M) ≅ ∏_{α∈𝕀} V(M_α), with arbitrary products. It is convenient to view a graded M_* simply as the family (M_α)_{α∈𝕀} of k-modules, and V(M_*) as the family (V(M_α)).

(2) Abelian-group gradings. If 𝕀 carries an abelian group structure, an 𝕀-grading on M amounts to an action of the diagonalizable group G = D(𝕀) = Spec k[𝕀]. Its points are A ↦ Hom_Ab(𝕀, A^*) ≅ Hom_{k-alg}(k[𝕀], A), where k[𝕀] is the group algebra.

(3) Choice of action. For the linear functor W(M): A ↦ M⊗A one has a choice of action, and V(M) gets the contragredient one. This continues on the next page.

Purpose: to define graded coalgebras (Δ(M_n) ⊂ Σ_{i+j=n} M_i⊗M_j) and graded algebra structures on V(M). Compatibility with the grading is equivalent to G-equivariance, and super-sign conventions come via 𝕀 → ℤ/2 (μ_2 → G). This is all preparation for divided-power algebras and coalgebras (Γ as the dual of Sym, etc.) in the de Rham setting.
errors: No mathematical errors. The equivalence of 𝕀-gradings with D(𝕀)-actions (k[𝕀]-comodule structures) is correct over any base ring k, without finiteness hypotheses.
The identification V(⊕M_α) = ∏V(M_α) is correct for arbitrary families, as the note says.

ideas.what: Grading of a module as a direct-sum decomposition, dually as a product decomposition of the functor V(M)=Hom(M,−)
ideas.modern_name: graded modules / quasi-coherent sheaves graded by a set; linear functors V(M)
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard; the V(M) formalism is in EGA I/II (𝕍(E)) and SGA 3
ideas.where_published: EGA I (1971 ed.) §9.4 / EGA II §1.7 for 𝕍(E); SGA 3 Exp. I

ideas.what: Gradings by an abelian group 𝕀 are equivalent to actions of the diagonalizable group D(𝕀)=Spec k[𝕀]; D(𝕀)(A)=Hom(𝕀,A^*)
ideas.modern_name: representations of diagonalizable groups = graded modules (comodules over the group algebra)
ideas.where_published: SGA 3 Exp. I 4.7.3 and Exp. VIII

ideas.what: Choice of action on W(M)=M⊗A versus the contragredient action on V(M)

deep.surprise_reason: Routine foundational set-up (gradings = diagonalizable group actions) that is fully covered in SGA 3. It is only preparation for the divided-power material.
transcription_corrections: First line: likely 'passent à la limite' (continuing 'les axiomes d'ass, d'unit, de comm.' from the previous page), not 'premier : le limite'.
The index set is a script/barred capital I (𝕀), not ℤ: 'Soit 𝕀 un ens.', '⊕_{α∈𝕀}', 'D(𝕀)', 'Hom_Ab(𝕀, A^*)', 'k(𝕀)'. ℤ appears only later as a special case.
'(produits [?] quelconques [?])' is plausibly '(produits quelconques)' or '(produits infinis)'.
'Il est sous-entendu comme aussi' is likely 'Il est commode ... de considérer aussi des graduations ... (M_* gradué) comme une famille (M_α)_{α∈𝕀} de k-modules'.
'le groupe diagonalisable Ĉ_n' is unclear. It is probably 'le groupe diagonalisable' followed by D(𝕀) defined on the next line; the hatted symbol may be 'Ĝ' or a notation for the dual group.
'Spec k(Z)' should read 'Spec k(𝕀)' (group algebra k[𝕀]), with 'Hom_{k-alg}(k(𝕀), A)' and the annotation 'algèbre de groupe'.
Bottom lines: roughly '[action] lin. sur M ... Et pour ce qu'on entend: sur W(M): A ↦ M⊗A, on a choix pour [l'action ...]', continuing to '... contragrédiente, sur V(M)' on the next page.
